title: Media presentations of Vietnam's cybersecurity law: A comparative approach with corpus-based critical discourse analysis

Justifying Vietnam's Cybersecurity Law: Powerlessness, Political Allegiance, and Alienation in State Media1 the Study Aims to Examine How Vietnam's Party-State and its State-Sponsored Media Justify the Promulgation and Enactment of the Controversial Cybersecurity Law. By Applying System Justification Theory (Sjt) and Positioning Theory (Pt), the Study Explores How State Media Exploit Cognitive Motives for System Justification by Portraying Powerless Laypeople (Sense of Powerlessness) Amidst Cyber Threats and Hostile Acts of Reactionary Forces (Political Alienation) in Contrast to the Powerful Leadership of the Party-State (Political Allegiance). The Study Also Examines How Political Leaders Invoke the Need for Closure/Orientation by Assigning Rights and Obligations to Involved Parties. To Achieve These Research Objectives, the Study Conducts a Critical Discourse Analysis (Cda) on 425
